mode: AERMOD distance profiles and separate analytical settling
limitations: Hypothetical source, normalized equal emitted mass; no measured AMP validation.
AERMOD is a local steady-state dispersion model; concentration is a period mean and deposition a period accumulation, not synchronous plume snapshots or particle trajectories.
Equivalent spheres do not resolve fibre orientation, polymer degradation, or fragmentation.
Equal mass emissions imply unequal emitted particle numbers across particle cases.
Receptor coverage and resolution constrain the displayed footprint; no long-range transport inference is supported.
AERMOD PERIOD concentration divides by noncalm, nonmissing modeled hours. Deposition sums processed one-hour deposits; missing/calm weather does not supply a validated full-calendar mass estimate.
A zero printed in a fixed-precision PLOTFILE can include a positive value below output precision; grey zero markers are not evidence of physical absence.
equation: v = (rho_p-rho_air) g d_ve^2 Cc(d_ve) / (18 mu chi)
shape_factor_caveat: Dynamic shape factor chi is a drag correction at fixed particle volume. Applying spherical Cunningham slip to nonspheres is approximate. Analytical chi changes do not alter any AERMOD run.

unassigned_morphotypes: Film: no defensible typical dynamic chi was verified for use as a universal atmospheric microplastic-film value; thickness, folding, orientation, and Reynolds/Knudsen regimes matter.
Foam: no defensible typical dynamic chi was verified; porosity, permeability, external shape, and effective density require separate characterization.
Irregular fragments and real fibers: published reference geometries are displayed, but the literature inspected does not establish one universally typical chi per microplastic morphotype.

source_ledger.description: Published aerosol reference geometries used as explicitly illustrative morphotype proxies; no numerical entry is an empirically typical chi for environmental microplastics.
source_ledger.definition: Dynamic shape factor chi is drag relative to a sphere of equal volume moving at the same speed in the specified flow regime. It is dimensionless and differs from Corey/Aschenbrenner factors, sphericity, and aspect ratio.

entries.label: Sphere / ideal bead: chi = 1.00
